title: Deduction of tax at source on payment of rent

effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Transitions to Section 393(1) Table 5 Item (i) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 effective 1 April 2026.

plainTextSummary: Any person (other than an individual or a HUF not subject to tax audit) paying any income by way of rent to a resident is required to deduct tax at source. Statutory Rates: (a) 2% for the use of any machinery, plant, or equipment; (b) 10% for the use of any land, building (including factory building), land appurtenant to a building, furniture, or fittings. Threshold: Tax is deductible only if the aggregate amount of rent credited or paid during the financial year exceeds ₹2,40,000. Non-PAN / Inoperative PAN penalty rate under Section 206AA is 20%. Under CBDT Circular 23/2017, where GST is separately stated in the invoice, TDS applies strictly on the basic rent excluding GST.

keyStatutoryThresholds.rentDefinitionScope: Any payment under any lease, sub-lease, tenancy, or other agreement for use of land, building, machinery, plant, equipment, furniture, or fittings, whether or not owned by payee.
keyStatutoryThresholds.cbdtCircular23GstExclusion: TDS applies strictly on basic rent excluding separately stated GST.

requiredDocumentChecklist: Executed Lease Agreement / Rent Agreement specifying premises or equipment and monthly rent
Cumulative Rent Ledger for current FY establishing date threshold of ₹2,40,000 was crossed
Rent invoice or debit note with GST separately broken out (if lessor is GST registered)
Lower deduction certificate under Section 197 / Section 395 (if lessor provides certificate)
